what_it_does: During language model inference, the model remembers (in the KV cache) every token it has seen so far to compute attention efficiently. But many of these cached tokens barely influence the final answer—their key-value pairs are almost irrelevant. This paper presents Sella, an LLM accelerator with a prediction engine that learns which KV pairs are low-value using cluster-based associative arrays (a compact data structure that groups similar keys). Once identified, the hardware can skip fetching low-value pairs from memory, cutting bandwidth and memory access overhead. The predictor learns a correlation pattern between query and key embeddings, so it catches useless KV pairs before they're read.
